title: Make undo of "Archive column" bring the board back

blocks.text: The team board has an "Archive column" button at the top of every column, and every edit on the board can be undone. Since archiving shipped, the bug reports say that undoing an archive sometimes empties the whole board, sometimes brings the columns back without their cards, and sometimes loses a card that was added just before the archive ran from the board's queue of pending edits.
`Board`, `History` and the board's own `archiveColumn(...)` and `restore(...)` work. Finish the two `TODO`s of `ArchiveColumn` in `src/main/java/practice/BoardCommands.java`:

items: `undo()`: put the board back as it was just before `execute()` ran.

blocks.text: The archive is kept sorted, so the order a column's cards had can't be read back from it. When you're done, undoing one archive, or several in turn, gives back every column with its cards in their order, and the archive as it was. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: archiving a column moves its cards into the sorted archive and leaves the other columns alone
two archive commands in a row archive the cards of both columns
after an undo, the columns the command did not archive still hold their cards
undo puts the archived cards back in their column, in order, and takes them out of the archive
undo of an archive command created before a card was added to the column brings that card back too

origin.section: Undo Restores What the Command Saved, So It Must Save a Copy Taken When It Runs

concepts: Copying a collection does not copy its mutable elements, so the snapshot copies every mutable level.
The copy is taken in execute(), because a command built earlier may run after other changes.
A command that saves a reference to the receiver's live state restores the changed state on undo; it must save a copy.
